dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:2701.text: Meat soup. From 肉; 賁 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2702.text: Meat soup. From 肉; 雋 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 纂.

shuowen:2703.text: A large piece of cut meat. From 肉; 𢦔 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2704.text: Thinly sliced meat. From 肉; 枼 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2705.text: Finely cut meat. From 肉; 會 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2706.text: Meat steeped or cured in liquid. From 肉; 奄 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2707.text: Small, soft and easily broken. From 肉 and abbreviated 絕.

shuowen:2708.text: Soft and easily broken. From 肉; 毳 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2709.text: Mixed meat. From 肉; 㪔 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2710.text: Cut meat. From 肉; 專 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2711.text: To pick meat from between bones. From 肉; 叕 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 啜 in the Odes' “Sobbing in tears.”

shuowen:2712.text: What is left after eating. From 肉; 仕 supplies the sound. The Changes says: “Biting dried leftover meat.”

shuowen:2713.text: To eat meat without becoming satisfied. From 肉; 臽 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 陷.

shuowen:2714.text: Dog meat. From 犬 and 肉. Pronounced like 然.

shuowen:2715.text: To rise or swell. From 肉; 眞 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2716.text: Sediment in meat juices. From 肉; 冘 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2717.text: To adhere closely; it is made from hides. From 肉; 翏 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2718.text: Some say it is the name of an animal and pictographic. The explanation is missing.

shuowen:2719.text: Flies breeding in meat. From 肉; 且 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2720.text: A small worm. From 肉; 囗 supplies the sound. Another explanation: empty.

shuowen:2721.text: Rotten. From 肉; 府 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2722.text: Flesh attached closely between bones. From 肉 and abbreviated 冎. Another explanation: bone without flesh.

shuowen:2723.text: Having much flesh. From 肉 and 卪.

shuowen:2724.text: Fat intestines. From 肉; abbreviated 啓 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2725.text: An infant's genitals. From 肉; 夋 supplies the sound. Alternatively from 血.

shuowen:2726.text: Hollow within. From 肉 and 空; 空 also supplies the sound.

shuowen:2727.text: 𦚧䏰, an insect name. Hanzhong has 𦚧䏰 county; many such insects occur underground there, hence its name. From 肉; 旬 supplies the sound. Considering its meaning, it should be written 潤蠢.

shuowen:2728.text: The insect 𦚧䏰. From 肉; 忍 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2729.text: The strength of flesh. From 力, 肉 and 竹; bamboo is a thing with many sinewy fibers. All graphs in this category contain 筋.

shuowen:2730.text: The base of a sinew. From 筋; abbreviated 夗 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2731.text: The cracking of finger and toe joints. From abbreviated 筋; 勺 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2732.text: A weapon. A pictograph. All graphs in this category contain 刀.

shuowen:2733.text: The grip of a knife. From 刀; 缶 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2734.text: The edge of a knife or sword. From 刀; 㖾 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2735.text: A sheath. Another explanation: to split. From 刀; 肖 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2736.text: A sickle. From 刀; 句 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2737.text: A large sickle. Another explanation: to rub or grind. From 刀; 豈 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2738.text: 剞𠜾, a curved knife. From 刀; 奇 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2739.text: The curved knife 剞𠜾. From 刀; 屈 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2740.text: Sharp. From 刀. Only after harmony comes benefit, hence from abbreviated 和. The Changes says: “Benefit is the harmony of righteousness.”

shuowen:2741.text: Sharp. From 刀; 炎 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2742.text: Beginning. From 刀 and 衣: the beginning of cutting clothing.

shuowen:2743.text: To cut evenly through. From 刀; 歬 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2744.text: To grade and mark out things. From 刀 and 貝; 貝 was the wealth of antiquity.

shuowen:2745.text: Firmly decisive. From 刀; 岡 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2746.text: To cut evenly. From 刀; 耑 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2747.text: To cut off. From 刀; 會 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2748.text: To cut. From 刀; 七 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2749.text: To cut. From 刀; 寸 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2750.text: To sever. From 刀; 嶭 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2751.text: To cut and wound. From 刀; 气 supplies the sound. Another explanation: to sever. Also pronounced like 㱯. Another explanation: when a knife is dull, grind it on tile or stone.

shuowen:2752.text: To wound with a sharp edge. From 刀; 歲 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2753.text: To carve. From 刀; 亥 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2754.text: To split. From 刀; 畐 supplies the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “A sacrifice with split and dismembered victims.”

shuowen:2755.text: To split. From 刀; 咅 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2756.text: To divide or distinguish. From 刀; 辡 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2757.text: To divide. From 刀; 半 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2758.text: To split. From 刀; 度 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2759.text: To split open. From 刀; 夸 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2760.text: To divide and separate. From 刀; 𡿪 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2761.text: To cut away. From 刀; 干 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2762.text: To cut away. From 刀; 叕 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2763.text: To cut away. From 刀 and 冊; 冊 is a written book.

shuowen:2764.text: To break or split. From 刀; 辟 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2765.text: To split or strip. From 刀 and 录; 录 means to carve and cut, and also supplies the sound.

shuowen:2766.text: To strip or cut away. From 刀; 害 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2767.text: To strip; to incise. From 刀; 𠩺 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2768.text: An awl-knife is called 劃. From 刀 and 畫; 畫 also supplies the sound.

shuowen:2769.text: To pick out and take. From 刀; 肙 supplies the sound. Another explanation: a hollow, 窐.

shuowen:2770.text: To scrape away diseased flesh from a sore. From 刀; 矞 supplies the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “The preparations for scraping and destroying diseased tissue.”

shuowen:2771.text: To make even. From 刀 and 齊; 齊 also supplies the sound.

shuowen:2772.text: To scrape. From 刀; abbreviated 㕞 supplies the sound. The Rites says: “A cloth wiping towel.”

shuowen:2773.text: To scrape or gather with the hand. From 刀; 𠯑 supplies the sound. [The expression 掊把 is uncertain.]

shuowen:2774.text: To pierce with a stone needle. From 刀; 𤐫 supplies the sound. Another explanation: 剽 means to rob people.

shuowen:2775.text: To stab. From 刀; 圭 supplies the sound. The Changes says: “The man stabs a sheep.”

shuowen:2776.text: To break and injure. From 刀; 坐 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2777.text: To cut off. From 刀; 喿 supplies the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Heaven thereby cuts off their mandate.”

shuowen:2778.text: To cut off. From 刀; 月 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2779.text: To strike. From 刀; 弗 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2780.text: To injure. From 刀; 桼 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2781.text: To sever. From 刀; 毚 supplies the sound. Another explanation: to cut or shave, 剽 and 釗.

shuowen:2782.text: To cut. From 刀; 元 supplies the sound. Another explanation: to make even.

shuowen:2783.text: To cut or shave. From 刀 and 金. The personal name of King Kang of Zhou.

shuowen:2784.text: To cut to shape. From 刀 and 未; 未 means things have matured and acquired flavor and can be cut. Another explanation: to stop.

shuowen:2785.text: A chip or flaw. From 刀; 占 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “A flaw in a white jade tablet.”

shuowen:2786.text: A lesser offense: without yet harming anyone with the knife, merely holding it and reviling someone still merits punishment. From 刀 and 詈.

shuowen:2787.text: To cut off an ear. From 刀 and 耳.

shuowen:2788.text: The punishment of cutting the nose. From 刀; 臬 supplies the sound. The Changes says: “Heaven will also cut off his nose.”

shuowen:2789.text: To cut the throat. From 刀; 幵 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2790.text: To cut the throat. From 刀; 坙 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2791.text: To reduce. From 刀; 尊 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2792.text: The Chu term for preparing fish. From 刀 and 魚. Pronounced like 鍥.

shuowen:2793.text: A contract. From 刀; 𢍏 supplies the sound. A document of divided contract tallies has notches cut at its side with a knife, hence called 契券.

shuowen:2794.text: A ruler killing a grandee is called 刺; 刺 means to wound directly. From 刀 and 朿; 朿 also supplies the sound.

shuowen:2795.text: To separate flesh from bone. From 刀; 易 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2796.text: To cut the throat. From 刀; 勿 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2797.text: To cut or scoop away. From 刀; 宛 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2798.text: Especially intense or severe. Its formation from 刀 is unexplained. 豦 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2799.text: A pillar. Its formation from 刀 is unexplained. Abbreviated 殺 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2800.text: The hard edge of a knife. It depicts a knife with an edge. All graphs in this category contain 刃.
